sections.content:
You know *antes de* and *después de* with an infinitive from A2 Unit 4, nominalization from B2 Unit 21, and the *pretérito perfecto* from A2 Unit 1 (*he firmado*). The perfect infinitive puts them together: *haber* + past participle (*haber firmado*). It names an action that is already complete, so it is the compact way to say "after", "because of" or "without having done something" in academic and legal prose.

It appears in two places. After a preposition: *tras haberlo leído*, *por haber firmado*, *sin haber respondido*, *al no haber recibido*. And as a noun, with *el* in front: *El haber firmado el acuerdo no lo obliga*. A pronoun attaches to *haber* (*haberlo leído*), and *no* goes before it (*por no haber firmado*). Use it when the doer is the same in both parts.

sections.title: The pattern
rows: Tras haberlo leído, cambió de opinión.
After reading it (having read it), he changed his mind.
Lo criticaron por haber firmado el acuerdo.
They criticised him for having signed the agreement.
Al no haber recibido respuesta, volvimos a escribir.
Since we had received no reply, we wrote again.
El haber firmado el acuerdo no lo obliga.
Having signed the agreement does not bind him.

items.spanish: Tras haber estudiado las dos muestras, el equipo confirmó la hipótesis.
items.english: After studying the two samples, the team confirmed the hypothesis.

items.spanish: La autora fue criticada por no haber contrastado sus fuentes.
items.english: The author was criticised for not having checked her sources.

items.spanish: Sin haber leído el informe completo, no se puede juzgar.
items.english: Without having read the whole report, one cannot judge.

items.spanish: El haber estudiado el tema no basta: hay que saber explicarlo.
items.english: Having studied the subject is not enough: you must be able to explain it.

sections.content: English uses *-ing* after a preposition: "after having read", "without answering". Spanish does not. A preposition takes the infinitive, so you say *tras haber leído*, not a form in *-ndo*. The simple infinitive is also possible when the order is obvious (*tras leer*, *sin responder*). The perfect infinitive is the usual choice when you want to stress that the action was finished first, and in *por no haber…* and *al no haber…*. The participle never changes: *haber firmado* is the same for singular, plural, masculine and feminine.
